doc.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Alive and Kicking, his first Broadway show
summary: Between the Diamond Horseshoe and Manhattan School, he plays a revue that closes after seven weeks.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: When we stopped off yesterday, we were in the early ’50s and you were going to the Manhattan School. When you were in school, you were also doing a lot of Broadway plays, weren’t you? You started at . . . .

For the most part – I did most of it during the time I was in the Diamond Horseshoe. Then I went into the theaters, and I was doing – I did a show called Alive and Kicking, which was the – that was the first show I ever did. That was a show – it had Jack Gilford, Carl Reiner, and David Burns. They were three of the principals. There were some others. I forget – I’m sorry I can’t remember the lady’s name, who was in the play. It was more of a revue. It wasn’t a typical Broadway show. It was called Alive and Kicking, and it was alive and kicking for only seven weeks. It closed after seven weeks.
This was the one that Noble Sissle allowed you to go . . . .
